items.prompt: Two proposed distinct families both list the exact ticker "ab" as their first member. What is wrong?

options.text: That ticker determines one canonical key, so the families should merge.
options.why: One original ticker cannot belong to two different sorted-letter equivalence classes.

options.text: This is valid because first members are ignored by grouping.
options.why: Canonical grouping is determined by each ticker, including the first member.

options.text: One family must rename the ticker to preserve distinct keys.
options.why: Changing input text is not part of the grouping contract.

options.text: The family count should be doubled to preserve the tie.
options.why: Counting the same equivalence class twice does not create a distinct family.

items.explanation: One original ticker cannot belong to two different sorted-letter equivalence classes.
